papers.title_en: From Interaction to Capability: Task Advancement as State and Supervision for GUI Agents
papers.authors: Ziyang Chen, Qian Li, Chengwei Qin
papers.evidence: GUI智能体通过可复用操作完成跨应用任务
papers.tldr: 长程跨应用GUI任务中，历史动作结果与可复用操作难以保留，失败尝试还会干扰有效经验。TAM把任务推进定义为经校验的进度，用推进状态指导后续执行，并在任务后监督抽象出可复用操作。MobileWorld上仅推进状态将成功率从12.0%提至28.2%，完整TAM相对最强基线提升17.6%并降38.7% token；SPA-Bench单应用英语Level 3达SOTA。
papers.abstract_en: GUI memory should preserve the results of past actions and learn reusable operations. This is difficult in long-horizon workflows, where agents must use information across applications and useful operations are interleaved with failed attempts. We introduce Task Advancement Memory (TAM), which defines task advancement as verified task progress, and supports ongoing task execution and learns reusable operations. During execution, Task Advancement State represents how verified task progress changes the remaining goals, allowing the agent to build on earlier achievements across applications. After each task, advancement supervision identifies and abstracts the interactions that produced a verified local result. The learned operations preserve the relation between required inputs, expected outcomes, and verification conditions. This retains locally successful operations from both successful and failed tasks. On MobileWorld GUI-only tasks, Advancement State alone raises success from 12.0% to 28.2%. Full TAM achieves a 17.6% relative gain in task success over the strongest evaluated baseline and reduces lifecycle tokens per solved task by 38.7%. On SPA-Bench, TAM achieves state-of-the-art task success in the single-app English Level 3 setting.

papers.title_en: Workflow-Aware Communication and Computation Scheduling for Mobile Edge AI Agents
papers.authors: Xingqiu He, Chaoqun You, Feng Wang, Zihan Chen, Shuai Wang, Jihong Park
papers.evidence: 移动边缘环境中的AI智能体通过多步工作流自主处理任务
papers.tldr: 移动边缘AI代理需执行动态生成的多步工作流，任务依赖在执行中逐步显现，给在线调度带来不确定性。论文用动态工作流图刻画部分已知流程，将加权完成时延目标转化为每时隙持有成本，并构建可计算的前瞻成本代理。算法据此决定计算放置，并按操作关键性在线分配无线资源块与边缘算力。仿真表明该方案在多场景优于基准，为动态代理工作流提供高效联合调度思路。
papers.abstract_en: AI agents are increasingly deployed in mobile edge environments to autonomously handle diverse tasks through multi-step workflows. Unlike conventional dependency-aware tasks with predefined dependency structures, agent workflows are dynamically generated based on intermediate execution results. To minimize the weighted sum of job completion latencies, this paper models partially revealed agent workflows using dynamic workflow graphs and formulates an online scheduling problem that jointly optimizes computation placement, wireless resource block allocation, and edge computing resource allocation. To address the uncertainty of future workflow evolution, we first transform the weighted completion time objective into an equivalent per-slot holding cost and characterize the optimal policy through a Bellman equation. We then construct a tractable look-ahead cost-to-go surrogate based on the revealed workflow and the estimated remaining latencies of active jobs. The proposed scheduling algorithm leverages the surrogate to determine computation placement and uses the resulting operation criticality to allocate wireless and edge computing resources online. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms the benchmark schemes across diverse scenarios.

papers.title_en: LeafSkill: Efficient Leaf-Level Action Grounding for Recursive LLM Agents
papers.authors: Shen Liu, Ze Zhou, Zhenguo Xu, Shaopu Wang, Yike Gao, Chunlei Wang
papers.evidence: 可复用的原子动作落地技术，支撑智能体执行任务
papers.tldr: 递归LLM智能体在分解长任务后，常为熟悉的原子子任务重复调用大模型完成动作落地。LeafSkill将叶级动作落地外置为可复用经验层，通过语义检索、模板绑定与1.7B选择器决定复用或回退原智能体。在Robotouille的200个任务上，它以68.5%成功率超过ReCAP的60.5%，并在共同完成任务上减少约14%的token与调用。表明可复用叶级落地能提升完成率并降低宿主模型推理开销，同时保留高层规划。
papers.abstract_en: Recursive large language model (LLM) agents solve long-horizon tasks through decomposition, execution, and environmental feedback. Yet after producing an atomic subtask, they often invoke the same large model again to translate a familiar instruction into an executable action. We observe that high-level planning is task-specific, whereas leaf-level action grounding recurs across tasks and can be checked against environment-admitted actions. We introduce LeafSkill, an external reuse layer that retrieves semantically related grounding experience, binds action templates to current objects and admissible actions, and uses a lightweight 1.7B selector to choose a bound action or defer the unchanged subtask to the original agent. Skills remain outside the model parameters, allowing a frozen selector to use post-training additions. Under lexical and syntactic paraphrases, exact matching retrieves none of the reference actions, while semantic retrieval preserves 96.0% and 97.0% candidate coverage; the frozen selector adopts 97.34% of unseen skill types. On an independent confirmation set of 200 Robotouille tasks, LeafSkill completes 137 tasks versus 121 for ReCAP (68.5% vs. 60.5%, exact McNemar p=.0259). On the 106 tasks completed by both, it reduces Qwen3.5-27B tokens by 14.42% and calls by 14.08%. A separate held-out repeat yields a consistent 9.0-point success gain and 18.98% token reduction. Reusable leaf grounding can thus improve task completion while reducing host-model inference without replacing high-level planning.

papers.title_en: Back to Basics: A Skill-Centric Approach to Generalist Web Agents
papers.authors: Minh Pham-Dinh, Md Farhan Ishmam, Hernan Yupanqui, Reaz Hassan Joarder, Kenneth Marino
papers.evidence: 技能中心网页智能体基准标注拖拽与手势等交互原语，可迁移至应用界面自动化
papers.tldr: 浏览器智能体缺乏对具体技能失败原因的诊断手段。作者构建含65个网站、369个任务的MiniWeb基准，标注37个可复用交互原语。又提出MiniWebGen自动生成技能训练数据，并用规划器组合技能完成整任务。微调后单技能成功率提升24.9pp，整任务在多个外部基准提升9.3至20.0pp。
papers.abstract_en: Browser agents do not just need more practice. They need to practice the right things. We introduce MiniWeb, a realistic miniature of the web comprising 65 interconnected websites across 15 domains, where agents navigate, search, and transact as people do. Its 369 human-annotated tasks cover everyday workflows and label 37 reusable interaction primitives grouped into 7 skill families, allowing us to diagnose which skills fail rather than only whether a task succeeds. Benchmarking ten open-weight agents, we find that drag & gesture is consistently the weakest family, with no agent solving more than 24% of its instances. To address this gap, we introduce MiniWebGen, a framework that autonomously generates verified, skill-centric training data from MiniWeb. Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-4B on just 3.1K verified trajectories improves single-primitive success by 24.9pp across 13 unseen websites, with gains across every skill family. However, these trajectories teach short-horizon interactions, which do not directly translate to full-task success. We build on this result with MiniWebAgent, which pairs the trained executor with a planner that decomposes full tasks into the skill-level steps it learned to perform. This approach improves task success by 19.4pp points on unseen MiniWeb sites and transfers to external benchmarks, with gains of 9.3pp on WebArena-Lite, 16.1pp on Online-Mind2Web, and 20.0pp on WebVoyager, without training on their trajectories. We provide a simple recipe for compact browser agents: practice reusable skills directly, then compose them to solve unfamiliar tasks.

papers.title_en: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization
papers.authors: Zishan Xu, Enjun Du, Mingqi Gao, Cheng Yang, Junhao Shen, Zirong Chen, Zhiyuan Yao, Yifu Guo, Yuquan Lu, Jinyang Huang, Zhengxi Lu, Siyi Liu, Ziyu Zheng, Yongqi Zhang, Difan Zou, Weiwen Liu
papers.evidence: 从系统层面分析智能体跨应用与工具执行委托任务
papers.tldr: 基础模型正从信息生成走向数字工作执行，但现有研究缺少对智能体可靠完成委托工作的统一视角。论文提出以工作为中心的系统级框架，将工作智能体视为基础模型与运行时执行环境的组合，并用工作持续性与开放性刻画条件、划分五类数字工作。基于此归纳五类核心能力，分析模型优化、执行环境优化及联合优化，并从工作成果角度审视评测方法与指标。该框架为理解、优化和评估工作智能体提供统一参考，指向可靠、可验证且有实际价值的工作交付。
papers.abstract_en: As foundation models evolve from information generation to digital work execution, agents are increasingly capable of completing complex tasks across tools, applications, and workflows. However, existing research lacks a unified perspective on how agents reliably accomplish delegated work. To address this gap, we present a work-centric, system-level perspective that views work agents as systems combining foundation models and runtime harnesses to execute tasks in stateful workspaces and deliver verifiable outcomes. We introduce two complementary dimensions, work persistence and work openness, to characterize working conditions, and classify digital work into five forms according to task scope and organization. Building on this framework, we identify five core capability families required for reliable work execution and examine approaches to model optimization, harness optimization, and their joint optimization. We further analyze existing evaluation methods and metrics from the perspective of work outcomes. Finally, we discuss future research directions, including sustained work delegation, adaptation to open environments, and the interaction between work execution and capability improvement. This paper provides a unified framework for understanding, optimizing, and evaluating work agents, supporting the development of systems capable of delivering reliable, verifiable, and practically valuable work outcomes.
